title: Nigeria's Index Ebola Patient Linked to Kenya Strain, Minister Says
summary: Genomic analysis shows Nigeria's first Ebola case is closely related to Kenya's index patient, according to Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate.
paragraphs: Genomic testing reveals that Nigeria's initial Ebola patient carries a viral strain closely resembling the first case reported in Kenya, according to Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate. The announcement follows the diagnosis of an Abuja resident who recently travelled from Uganda.

The affected individual is married to an employee at the Swiss embassy in Abuja. Although official reports from Uganda previously claimed she visited the Democratic Republic of Congo, Switzerland's foreign ministry denied this. Health officials suspect possible exposure at an airport while traveling.

Nigeria is now the fourth nation in Africa impacted by the Bundibugyo strain outbreak, alongside the DRC, Uganda, and Kenya. Based on World Health Organization statistics, the continent-wide epidemic has recorded more than 9,700 confirmed cases and 4,690 deaths as of October.
